decision: Render each cover on the publisher's machine. A zero-dependency CDP client launches the user's own Chrome, Chromium or Edge headless over --remote-debugging-pipe. That browser loads a cover page that ships inside the relic-mcp package, built at relic-mcp build time from relic-viewer's own renderer modules, served through CDP Fetch interception on the non-resolvable origin https://cover.relic.invalid, with network egress closed by browser flags. Audio and video are decoded by the optional ffmpeg the client already probes for. The finished 1200x630 PNG or JPEG goes up through a new token-authorized POST /api/relics/{id}/cover that validates it strictly and stores it at m/cover/{id}/{sha256}. It is served at /{id}/cover/{sha256}.{png|jpg}, and og:image points at it only while it depicts the live, current version. Otherwise og:image stays card.v1.png byte for byte.
rejected: Option (a), a render page served by the deployed server and fed plaintext over CDP. It hands the publish path server-supplied code holding the whole plaintext. That is the unreversed locked constraint frame.md:13 ('the server hands the agent no code to run, and that half stands unreversed'), restated in README.md:316-322 and publish.ts:9-12. It also widens Jason's authorized leak from first-screen pixels to the entire file under operator intent. A compromised server could exfiltrate by navigation, and it would control the page's CSP too.
Option (b), the real viewer at the full link. Same violation, plus it calls /api/relics/{id}/mint (spends opens and download cap) and needs the key in a URL handed to a browser.
Playwright or Puppeteer: they break the zero-runtime-dependency package (relic-mcp/package.json has no dependencies field; engines node>=18).
Server-side rendering: the server would need plaintext.
Pure-Node rasterizers (satori, resvg, canvas): they are runtime dependencies and cannot run HTML, JSX or PDF the way the viewer does.
Auto-downloading a browser: a runtime download of executable code, which conflicts with the provenance and readable-source posture (README.md:289-299).

code_facts: frame.md:13 locked constraint 1, unreversed for the publish path; README.md:316-322 explains why a server-returned script is rejected.
relic-mcp ships zero runtime deps; index.ts:5-7 claims plain Node from 18; build.ts:42-44 uses define for build-time constants (process.env.RELIC_MCP_VERSION, read at server.ts:1342).

On Node 18/20 probeFfmpeg's try/catch swallows the TypeError and silently reports ffmpeg absent [INFERENCE from reading; Node 18/20 not run].

Fetch.fulfillRequest serves https://cover.relic.invalid pages, a module worker loaded by URL (/static/w.js) and a blob-URL worker, all with --host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND and a dead proxy in place.

JPEG q85 markers are APP0, APP2 (ICC), DQT, DQT, SOF0, DHT x4, SOS, so APP2 must be stripped before upload.
Legibility: a 17px serif prose sample at 600x315 CSS @2x renders crisp, with body text 34 image px (about 14 px at a 500 px unfurl). PNG 170,730 B; JPEG q85 64,328 B.
Sandboxed srcdoc frame (sandbox=allow-scripts) with a meta CSP: document.write'd HTML runs scripts, and a blob: module import works.

Egress, hostile HTML with no CSP at all aimed at a loopback collector (fetch, img, stylesheet, preconnect, sendBeacon, WebSocket, EventSource, delayed frame navigation, localhost variants): zero HTTP/TCP arrivals. Dropping the proxy alone still gave zero, and dropping the resolver rule alone still gave zero, so each layer is independently sufficient for HTTP-family traffic.

WebRTC STUN leaked (3 UDP packets) with --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy, with meta CSP "webrtc 'block'", with Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline, and with --disable-blink-features=RTCPeerConnection. It went to zero with --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp (loopback and LAN 10.4.1.26, two runs each) or with the profile pref webrtc.ip_handling_policy.
Page-session Fetch interception with pattern '*' never saw any request from the sandboxed srcdoc frame. Interception is an asset server, not containment.

A single Fetch.fulfillRequest body of 64 MiB works (600 ms in page). At 100 MiB Chrome closed the pipe (EPIPE), and the unhandled stream error crashed the Node host process. 7 x 16 MiB parts assembled to 100 MiB in 1.68 s.

1_render_engine.decision: Use the publisher's system Chrome, Chromium or Edge, launched headless per cover over --remote-debugging-pipe by a zero-dependency CDP client in relic-mcp. One browser per publish call, a fresh 0700 temp profile removed after. Never pass --no-sandbox.
discovery: deps seam: the renderer factory takes chromePath. undefined discovers; 'none' or 'disabled' -> skipped reason browser_disabled.

Env override RELIC_CHROME_PATH (mirrors RELIC_FFMPEG_PATH). 'none'|'disabled' -> browser_disabled. Any other value must be an executable file, else skipped browser_not_found with detail 'RELIC_CHROME_PATH points at

, which is not an executable file'. Discovery does not continue after a bad explicit value.

darwin, in order: /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome, ~/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome, /Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium, /Applications/Microsoft Edge.app/Contents/MacOS/Microsoft Edge, /Applications/Google Chrome Canary.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome Canary.

linux, PATH lookup in order: google-chrome-stable, google-chrome, chromium, chromium-browser, microsoft-edge-stable, microsoft-edge, chrome-headless-shell; then /opt/google/chrome/chrome, /snap/bin/chromium.
All platforms, after the defaults: PATH lookup of chrome-headless-shell and chromium.
Binaries whose basename contains 'headless-shell' get --headless; everything else gets --headless=new.
1_render_engine.when_absent: Publish and republish always complete. structuredContent.cover = {status:'skipped', reason:'browser_not_found', detail:'No Chrome, Chromium, or Edge was found on this machine (looked in: <list>). Set RELIC_CHROME_PATH to one to render covers.'}. The text result says 'Cover image: none. <detail> Link previews show the generic Relic card.' No cover request is sent and og:image stays card.v1.png. Launch failures (crash, root without sandbox, no CDP answer inside the startup timeout) -> browser_failed with the last 2 KB of Chrome stderr in detail. Chrome stderr is captured into a bounded buffer and never written to the MCP process's stderr.

2_render_page.decision: Option (c). The cover page source lives in relic-viewer (packages/relic-viewer/src/cover/) and reuses its renderer modules: renderMarkdown, highlightCode, transpileJsx, sandbox.ts, styles.css and pdfjs-dist. A new buildCover({outdir}) in relic-viewer/build.ts emits it, and only relic-mcp/build.ts calls it, into packages/relic-mcp/dist/cover/. It is never written into relic-viewer/dist, so the service origin can never serve it. relic-mcp serves the files to Chrome through Fetch interception on https://cover.relic.invalid. The plaintext reaches the page only through that interception, so nothing leaves the machine.
2_render_page.html_jsx: No usercontent origin. The cover page hosts the frame itself: <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" srcdoc=frame.html>. frame.html is public/sandbox.html with the unminified sandbox.ts bundle inlined and the frame CSP as the first head element. The sandbox.ts protocol is reused unchanged.
2_render_page.csp_and_egress: The page CSP arrives as a fulfilled response header and the frame CSP as a meta tag. Containment of relic content rests on browser flags, because interception cannot see the isolated sandboxed frame (measured). The flags are: --host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND, --proxy-server=http://proxy.relic.invalid:1, --proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>, --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp, --disable-quic. Every fulfilled response carries cache-control: no-store so no plaintext lands in Chrome's disk cache.
2_render_page.version_skew: The cover renderer is pinned to the npm client build. The server contract is only the upload endpoint and the og tags, both format-agnostic. Old client with new server: no covers, card. New client with old server: POST returns a non-problem 404, reported as skipped service_unsupported. Release the server first.

4_upload.decision: A separate JSON POST /api/relics/{id}/cover, authorized by publish_token in the body (the republish precedent), sent after the ciphertext PUT and complete. It is not inline in the grant, because a failed publish must never leave a plaintext cover behind and an old server must be detectable (404). It is not a signed GCS PUT, because the server must validate before anything is stored or served.
4_upload.ordering_publish: render (local, before encrypt and grant) -> encrypt -> grant -> PUT ciphertext -> complete -> savePublishState(cover_uploaded:false) -> POST cover -> if uploaded, savePublishState(cover_uploaded:true). If the second write fails the publish still succeeds, and the text says the local cover record was not updated.
4_upload.ordering_republish: digest -> duplicate gate (table below; may render first) -> render -> comment gate -> encrypt -> republish grant (server clears and deletes the old cover) -> PUT -> complete -> save state -> POST cover for the new version -> update state.
4_upload.validation: Shared validateCoverRaster in @relic/format/cover, which the client also runs before upload. The client strips PNG ancillary chunks and JPEG APP1-APP15/COM before upload.
4_upload.storage: m/cover/{id}/{sha256}, content-type set, no lifecycle rule, soft-delete applies. Row field cover (contract below).

5_serving.decision: GET|HEAD /{id}/cover/{sha256}.{png|jpg}, content-addressed. Republish changes the URL, so unfurl caches refresh. cache-control is public, max-age=86400 rather than immutable, so a takedown's tail in honoring caches is bounded to a day; a content-addressed URL never needs revalidation for correctness. The route mints nothing and touches no counter.
5_serving.lifecycle: New version: beginVersion clears row.cover, then the handler deletes every m/cover/{id}/* object. Decline is a republish without upload. Tombstone: operatorDelete deletes every cover object and reports covers_deleted. Expiry: the shell and cover route stop serving at once, and the object stays until a deletion, matching ciphertext behavior (bucket comment resource.google_storage_bucket.relics.tf:11-17). Deleted objects sit in soft delete per the existing policy.
5_serving.fallback: card.v1.png with today's exact tags when there is no row, a tombstone, expiry, no cover, cover.version !== row.version, or the store throws.

7_guards_and_proof.replacement_guarantee: The service serves exactly two kinds of raster: /assets/card.v1.png, and a cover that a live row references for its current version and that passed validateCoverRaster. A declined cover leaves nothing in the row, the store or any URL.
guards: G1 server, app.test.ts: a state table (no cover, declined, stale version, tombstoned, expired, unknown id, store throws, hash mismatch, extension mismatch) -> the shell og:image is card.v1.png and the cover route returns 404. Mutation proofs: drop the cover.version === row.version check, then drop the tombstone check in the cover route; each must fail a named case.

G2 format, cover.test.ts: the validator rejects a PNG+ZIP polyglot (trailing bytes), a tEXt chunk, 1200x631, interlaced, 16-bit, a bad CRC, oversized IDAT, JPEG with COM, JPEG with APP1, JPEG with bytes after EOI, and wrong JPEG dims. Mutation: remove the trailing-data check, and the polyglot case must fail.

G3 declined leaves nothing. Server: republish without upload -> row.cover undefined, listCovers(id) empty, the old URL 404. Client: cover:false -> zero renderCover calls and zero /cover requests. Mutation: make beginVersion keep cover, and the server case must fail.

G4 renderer containment: chromeArgs is pinned by an exact-list test, and the cover-path egress collector must see zero arrivals. Mutation: drop --webrtc-ip-handling-policy -> the list test fails, and the collector sees UDP (measured).
G5 the service never serves the renderer: relic-viewer dist/ contains none of the cover files, and GET /assets/cover.js returns 404.
Every worker runs its mutations and names the failing test in the PR body.
7_guards_and_proof.datastore_proof: cover-path.ts and app.test.ts assert row.cover === undefined, store.listCovers(id) has length 0, and every previously issued cover URL returns 404 after a cover:false republish. gcsstore.test.ts asserts deleteCovers lists m/cover/{id}/ and issues a DELETE per object plus a CAS clear.
7_guards_and_proof.e2e: packages/relic-mcp/test/cover-path.ts (contract below), plus a production probe and PATH.md entries.

contracts.validation_rules: length 0 or > COVER_CAP_BYTES -> size. PNG: 8-byte signature; every chunk length within bounds and its CRC valid (crc); the first chunk is IHDR, length 13, 1200x630 (dimensions), bit depth 8, color type 2 or 6, compression 0, filter 0, interlace 0 (structure). Only IHDR, then one or more contiguous IDAT, then IEND of length 0, are allowed (chunk). Zero bytes after IEND (trailing_data). Inflated IDAT length is exactly 630*(1+1200*bpp) with bpp 3 or 4, and every row's filter byte is 0..4 (pixel_data). JPEG: SOI; markers allowed before SOS are APP0 (once, 'JFIF\0'), DQT, SOF0 or SOF2 (exactly one, precision 8, height 630, width 1200, components 1 or 3), DHT, DRI. Then SOS, entropy data with FF00 stuffing and RST0-7, further DHT/SOS for progressive, and EOI as the last two bytes (trailing_data). Any other marker (APP1-15, COM) -> chunk.
contracts.row_and_store:
store.ts: export interface RelicCover { readonly version: number; readonly sha256: string /* lowercase hex of stored bytes */; readonly type: CoverType; readonly kind: CoverKind; readonly bytes: number; readonly uploadedAt: number }
RelicRow gains: cover?: RelicCover | undefined
RelicStore gains:
  putCover(id: string, cover: RelicCover, bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<'stored' | 'stale_version' | 'not_found'>
  getCoverBytes(id: string, sha256: string): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>
  listCovers(id: string): Promise<readonly string[]>   // sha256 of every stored object for id
  deleteCovers(id: string): Promise<number>            // deletes every object, clears row.cover by CAS, returns the count
beginVersion (both stores) also sets cover: undefined.
GCS object key: `${storePrefix}/cover/${id}/${sha256}` (production m/cover/{id}/{sha256}), uploadType=media with content-type = cover.type. getCoverBytes uses ?alt=media; listCovers uses a names-only list of prefix `${storePrefix}/cover/${id}/`.
putCover (GCS) sequence: write the object, then mutateRelic. If row.version !== cover.version, return 'stale_version' and delete the just-written object; if there is no row, return 'not_found'. Otherwise set row.cover, then delete the other objects under the prefix. MemoryStore: Map<id, Map<sha256, {bytes, type}>> with identical semantics.
contracts.upload_endpoint:
POST /api/relics/{id}/cover
Request: content-type application/json; body over 720,000 bytes (by content-length, or by a capped streamed read) -> invalid_cover failure size.
{ "publish_token": string, "version": integer, "kind": CoverKind, "type": "image/png" | "image/jpeg", "data": string /* RFC 4648 base64, padded, /^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/, length % 4 === 0 */ }
Check order: killSwitchEngaged -> service_paused; limiter.check(`cover ${ip}`, config.publishRateLimit) -> publish_rate_limited; parseRelicId -> invalid_relic_id; tombstone -> relic_removed; row -> relic_not_found; body cap and JSON -> invalid_cover (size | structure); sha256Hex(publish_token) timingSafeEqual row.publishTokenHash -> invalid_publish_token; version !== row.version -> cover_version_stale (extensions relic_id, current_version); storage.stat(objectKey(id, version)) absent -> relic_not_yet_published; isCoverKind and COVER_TYPES -> invalid_cover structure; base64 -> invalid_cover structure; decoded length > config.coverCapBytes -> invalid_cover size (size_limit_bytes); validateCoverRaster(bytes, inflateSync) -> invalid_cover <failure>; the declared type must match the detected type -> invalid_cover signature; store.putCover -> stale_version -> cover_version_stale | not_found -> relic_not_found.
200: { "relic_id": string, "version": number, "kind": CoverKind, "type": CoverType, "sha256": string, "bytes": number, "cover_url": "<serviceOrigin>/<id>/cover/<sha256>.<png|jpg>" }
problems.ts: add invalid_cover 400 'Invalid cover image', cover_version_stale 409 'Cover is for a version that is no longer current'. ProblemExtensions: cover_validation_failure?: CoverValidationFailure; current_version?: number.
config.ts: coverCapBytes: COVER_CAP_BYTES (imported from @relic/format/cover, like PLAINTEXT_CAP_BYTES).
contracts.serve_route:
Router (app.ts handle, before the final 404): segments.length === 3 && segments[1] === 'cover' && head is not reserved && method GET|HEAD -> coverRoute(head, segments[2]).
Name must match /^([0-9a-f]{64})\.(png|jpg)$/. Check order: parseRelicId, tombstone, row, expiry, row.cover present, cover.version === row.version, sha256 equal, extension === coverExtension(type), getCoverBytes. Any miss -> 404, body 'Not found', headers cache-control: no-store, x-content-type-options: nosniff, x-robots-tag: noindex. A store error -> 503 with cache-control: no-store.
200 headers exactly: content-type: <cover.type>; content-length: <n>; cache-control: public, max-age=86400; x-content-type-options: nosniff; referrer-policy: no-referrer; x-robots-tag: noindex; content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox. No content-encoding. HEAD: same headers, null body.
Never calls mint, markPublished, consumeMint, rememberMint or appendMintLog.
contracts.shell_og:
When there is no tombstone, the row exists, the relic is not expired, and row.cover?.version === row.version:
  og:image and twitter:image = `${serviceOrigin}/${canonicalId}/cover/${cover.sha256}.${coverExtension(cover.type)}`
  og:image:type = cover.type; og:image:width = 1200; og:image:height = 630; og:image:alt = COVER_ALT[cover.kind]
Otherwise today's tags, byte for byte. Tag order unchanged.

contracts.page_protocol:
Virtual origin https://cover.relic.invalid. Node handles Fetch.requestPaused (pattern '*', stage Request): /index.html, /cover.js, /cover.css, /styles.css, /frame.html, /pdf.worker.mjs from assetDir; /input/{i} = bytes.subarray(i*16 MiB, (i+1)*16 MiB); anything else -> Fetch.failRequest errorReason BlockedByClient. Every fulfilled response carries cache-control: no-store and a content-type by extension (.html text/html; charset=utf-8, .js/.mjs text/javascript; charset=utf-8, .css text/css; charset=utf-8, input application/octet-stream).
index.html additionally carries content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' blob:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; media-src data: blob:; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'
frame.html, first head element: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline' blob:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; media-src data: blob:; worker-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'">
Node CDP sequence: Target.createTarget {url:'about:blank'}; Target.attachToTarget {targetId, flatten:true}; on that session: Fetch.enable; Page.enable; Runtime.enable; Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride {width:600,height:315,deviceScaleFactor:2,mobile:false}; Emulation.setEmulatedMedia {features:[{name:'prefers-color-scheme',value:'light'},{name:'prefers-reduced-motion',value:'reduce'}]}; Page.navigate {url:'https://cover.relic.invalid/index.html'}; wait for Page.loadEventFired; Runtime.evaluate 'window.__relicCover && window.__relicCover.protocol' must equal 1, else render_failed 'cover renderer assets are from a different build'; Runtime.evaluate `window.__relicCover.render(${JSON.stringify(request)})` with awaitPromise and returnByValue -> CoverRenderResult; if ok, Page.captureScreenshot {format:'png', captureBeyondViewport:false}. No Runtime binding: render completion comes only from the main-world evaluate, so frame content cannot spoof it.
Page API (cover.js module, assigned synchronously at top level): window.__relicCover = { protocol: 1, render(request: CoverRenderRequest): Promise<CoverRenderResult> }. Input bytes: fetch('/input/0'..'/input/{parts-1}'), joined into new Blob(parts, {type: input.mimetype}). Every kind ends with await document.fonts.ready and two requestAnimationFrame ticks. html and jsx: fetch('/frame.html') text as srcdoc; post relic:render or relic:render-jsx after relic:sandbox-ready; wait for relic:tree; then FRAME_SETTLE_MS. pdf: GlobalWorkerOptions.workerPort = new Worker('/pdf.worker.mjs', {type:'module'}) created lazily, never via pdf.ts.
Encode ladder (src/cover/raster.ts): PNG -> normalizePng (keep IHDR/IDAT/IEND) -> validateCoverRaster; if bytes <= COVER_CAP_BYTES, use it. Else JPEG q85 -> normalizeJpeg (drop APP1-15, COM) -> validate; else JPEG q70; else skipped over_size_budget. A validation failure on our own output -> render_failed.

what_would_prove_this_wrong: cover-path egress collector records any arrival. The containment is incomplete, so stop and come back.
The ubuntu-latest google-chrome cannot launch headless with its sandbox ('No usable sandbox'). The only acceptable fix is a CI-only sysctl; never --no-sandbox in product code.
Bun 1.3.14 (CI pin) or Node 18/20 cannot carry the fd 3 and 4 pipes (measured only on Bun 1.4.2 and Node 24).
Chrome's screenshot PNG is not 8-bit RGB/RGBA non-interlaced on Linux or Edge. The validator would refuse our own output.
pdfjs's real worker or React's mount fails inside the cover page or srcdoc frame. Only a trivial worker and a blob module import were measured.
Fetch fulfillment of the .invalid origin fails on another Chromium-family build in the discovery list.
Unfurlers reject or crop the cover. Real Slack and iMessage behavior is unmeasured until Jason pastes a link.
risks_and_unknowns: Privacy posture: default-on means the operator, unfurl services and anyone with the link minus the fragment see every relic's first screen unless the agent declines. The tool text must carry this.
Removing a cover requires a republish, which the comment gate blocks until open comments are addressed (the addresses parameter clears them in the same call). Operator takedown remains.
Republish deletes the old cover, so an unfurler that cached the old shell shows a broken image until its own cache expires.
Egress: covers of up to 512 KiB per unfurl fetch are served by Cloud Run with no CDN, against the 35.7 KB immutable card.
Abuse: public plaintext images under relik.link. They are bounded by validation, deletion and the 1-day cache, and still a new surface.

npm tarball grows by the unminified cover assets (pdf.worker.mjs is 1.89 MB unminified per unpkg; plus pdfjs main, React and sucrase). README's readable-source claim must be restated to include vendored third-party code in dist/cover.
Covers follow viewer routing, so WebP and ICO get no cover until the sniffer learns them; zip-based Office files show their XML parts.
Covers can differ run to run (fonts, JS timing). The duplicate gate keys on cover presence, not cover bytes.

Unverified: Windows pipe transport and discovery; Chrome below 112 with --headless=new; snap Chromium's private /tmp; root containers (Chrome refuses without --no-sandbox, so covers are skipped with that reason).
side_findings: Measured, outside this scope: Chrome 155 does not enforce CSP "webrtc 'block'". A URL-loaded sandboxed frame served the production directive list as a header (app.ts:310-325 shape) still sent 5 STUN packets to an author-chosen address. Relic HTML can therefore learn a recipient's IP, which contradicts the closing-egress posture (README.md:49). The fix is not a header.
Pre-existing: Promise.withResolvers in resolve-anchor.ts (177, 224) breaks ffmpeg on Node 18-21 despite engines >=18. C2 fixes it and adds a guard.
